name: Handler
subcategory: AI marketing agent for indie apps
tagline: An AI agent that plans and drafts marketing content for solo app makers who would rather be coding.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: The mechanical part of this is a prompt chain: read the product's landing page, infer positioning, output a content calendar and a pile of channel-specific drafts. An agent can build that in an afternoon and it will produce output that looks roughly as good as any generic tool's, because the underlying model is the same one everybody rents. Where the DIY version falls down is everything after the draft: actual posting, OAuth to X and LinkedIn and Reddit, scheduling that survives your laptop closing, and any feedback loop that tells you which post did anything. The harder thing to clone is not the code but the opinion, whatever prompt scaffolding and channel playbooks the vendor has tuned over hundreds of launches, and you will be guessing at that. Build it if you mainly want drafts on demand; pay if you want something that actually ships posts without you.
coreLoopDIY: A local CLI that ingests your app's landing page, writes a positioning brief, then generates a 30 day content calendar with channel-specific post drafts you review and export.
requirements: A live landing page or a paragraph describing the product
Your own accounts if you ever want to actually publish anything
whatYouLose: Automatic publishing and scheduling: your version stops at the draft
Channel playbooks tuned on launches that were not yours
Any attribution or analytics loop telling you what worked
A hosted scheduler that runs when your laptop is shut
Someone else's taste, which is the part you are actually short on
moatNotes: The defensible bits are prompt taste and the unglamorous OAuth plumbing to a dozen social APIs, not the generation itself.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because marketing is the work app makers avoid, and a tool that hands you a filled calendar and posts it for you removes the excuse. A self-built drafter still requires you to open it, read the output, decide, and paste into five sites, which is exactly the friction that made you skip marketing in the first place. Paying for the hosted version outsources the nagging as much as the writing.
notes: Generating marketing copy is the easy half; the hard half is being the kind of person who publishes it.
prompt:
Build a local CLI tool called "handy" that plans marketing content for a single software product.

Stack, no substitutions: Node 20, TypeScript, commander for the CLI, better-sqlite3 for storage, undici for fetch, the Anthropic Messages API for generation. No web server, no frontend, no accounts, no telemetry.

Setup: read ANTHROPIC_API_KEY from .env via dotenv. Store everything in ./handy.db. Commit a .env.example, never a real key.

Commands:
1. handy init --url URL : fetch the page, strip tags and scripts to plain text, cap at 20k chars, save as the product record. Also accept --describe "text" instead of a URL.
2. handy brief : send the product text to the model and store a positioning brief as JSON: audience, top three pains, three differentiators, tone rules, five banned phrases, three proof gaps. Print it as markdown.
3. handy plan --days 30 --channels x,reddit,linkedin,newsletter : generate a dated calendar of post ideas, each with channel, angle, hook, and which brief pain it targets. Store one row per idea.
4. handy draft [--id N | --all] : for each idea, generate a channel-native draft respecting per-channel length limits (x: 280 chars, reddit: 250 words and no marketing voice, linkedin: 150 words, newsletter: 400 words). Store drafts with a status column: draft, approved, rejected.
5. handy review : interactive loop through pending drafts, keys a/r/e to approve, reject, or open in $EDITOR.
6. handy export --out ./out : write approved drafts as dated markdown files plus a calendar.md index.

Rules: every model call goes through one wrapper with retries and a token log printed at exit. Deterministic prompt templates live in ./prompts/*.md so they can be edited without touching code. Refuse to invent metrics, customer names, or testimonials, and say so explicitly in the system prompt.

Explicitly out of scope: publishing to any social network, OAuth, scheduling daemons, analytics, image generation, multi-product support.

Deliver: working code, a README with a five command quickstart, and one seeded example run using --describe so it can be tested without a live site.
